docs.task: How the plan document's checks run and report warnings per phase and step.

asks: How the plan document's checks run.
How they report warnings per phase and per step.

data_flow.step: The plan agent calls the Document tool with `document` or `update`/`remove`; the tool resolves the path, checks the name prefix `ostra-plan-` and that it is not a `-phase-` file, merges updates with `doc::apply_update`.

`doc::write(kind, &md, &value)` parses the JSON with `DocKind::parse` (schema errors abort the write; for a plan it also fills each phase's `skills` from its steps, Rule P7), then calls `check(&document)` on the typed PlanDoc.

`check` dispatches to `plan()`: question checks, `plan_skills`, unique phase ids, P10 sequence, then per phase the depends_on and deliverable checks and `phase_body`, which checks P12, steps non-empty, unique step ids, step id shape, P11, P13, P5. Then cycle detection. `Issues::done` sorts errors first.
`write` stores the JSON, renders the master markdown and one phase file pair per phase, deletes stale phase files, and returns `Written { document, files, issues }`. Issues are not persisted.
The tool formats the result in `summary`: a 'Wrote the plan: N phases, M steps, K clarifying questions.' line, the file list, and the issue lines. This text is what the agent sees.

At submit, `check_submit` reloads the stored JSON via `read_doc`, runs `blocking` which keeps only Error-level issues, and refuses the submit if any exist. Warnings never block. It then compares the submit's `step_count`, `phases`, and per-phase fields with the document.

For the browser, `load_view` re-parses the stored JSON and calls `check` again (for a phase file it builds `Document::Phase(PhaseDoc)` so only `phase_body` rules run), returning `DocumentView { document, issues }`. The web `buildMarks` keys each issue by `normId(element)` and shows warnings with tone `warn` on the matching phase or step element, or on the overview if the element is null.

patterns.description: Every rule calls `out.error(element, message)` or `out.warn(element, message)`. The element is a free-text label: `phase {id}` for phase-level issues, `step {id}` for step-level issues, `None` for document-level issues. Messages start with the instruction, then the reason in a `because` clause, per the repo prose rules, and cite the rule ID in parentheses where one exists. `done()` stable-sorts by level so errors come before warnings; order within a level is the order rules ran.
patterns.name: Issue collection with a labelled element

patterns.description: `check` matches on Document. For a `Plan`, `plan()` runs clarifying-question checks, `plan_skills` (P6/P7 errors), unique phase ids, the P10 sequence check, then loops over phases: `depends_on` checks, a deliverable-index warning, and `phase_body(p, out)`. For a `Phase` document (one phase file loaded in the browser), `phase_file` calls only `phase_body`. Therefore a rule placed in `phase_body` appears on both the master plan view and the phase file view; a rule placed in `plan()` appears only on the master plan view.
patterns.name: Plan check composition: plan-level rules, then phase_body per phase

patterns.description: Plan warnings today, all in check.rs: (1) phase `depends_on` names a phase with id >= this one (element `phase N`, in `plan`); (2) a phase's deliverable is not in `deliverables` when `deliverables` is non-empty (element `phase N`, in `plan`); (3) a step with empty `delivers` (P11, element `step N.M`, in `phase_body`); (4) a delivered requirement id not in the phase's `requirements` (element `step N.M`, in `phase_body`). Plan errors are: missing test rationale (P12), zero steps, step id not `{phase}.{n}`, binding rule not in `constraints` or not verbatim or empty (P13), empty `verify` (P5), phase id sequence (P10), nonexistent depends_on, cycles, skills (P6, P7), duplicate ids. No existing rule inspects the number of steps in a phase or the `size` of a step.
patterns.name: Existing per-phase and per-step warnings

document.problem: The plan agent writes a typed PlanDoc through the Document tool, and Ostra runs `check` on every write. Issues come back as a flat list of DocIssue values (level, optional element label, message), and warnings do not block submit. This document records where plan checks live, how phase and step issues are labelled and reported, and what already exists around phase and step size, so a change that adds a phase-level warning can follow the existing pattern.

submit.findings_summary: The check code is `check()` in crates/ostra-core/src/doc/check.rs. For a plan it runs `plan()`, which calls `phase_body()` per phase. Issues are DocIssue values with a level, an optional element label (`phase N` or `step N.M`) and a message, and errors sort first. The check runs on every Document tool write (`store::write`, formatted by `summary` in ostra-tools/src/doc.rs) and again in `store::load_view` for the browser. `check_submit` blocks only on errors, so warnings never block. Four plan warnings exist today (depends_on on a later phase, deliverable missing from the index, step without `delivers`, delivered requirement not quoted in the phase). No rule inspects the step count of a phase or a step's `size`. The plan prompt's 'Warnings:' bullet (assets/agents/plan/prompt.md:486) and docs/internals/pipeline.md would need to change with any new warning, and the plan fixture must keep producing zero issues.

patterns.description: Size is stated in four places, all in `assets/agents/plan/prompt.md`. (1) Step 3 ties the number of steps to the stakes level: Low is 3 to 5 steps, Medium 5 to 15, High 10 to 30. These ranges count steps for the whole change, not per phase. (2) Step 5 rule P2 makes a step exactly one file, and the Definitions table calls a step 'one atomic unit: one file, one action, one verification command'. (3) The step field table has a `size` field of `Small`, `Medium`, or `Large`, with no definition of the three values beyond the names. The prompt says this step size is separate from the phase `complexity` tier (P9), and the code stores it as `StepSize`. (4) The phase is defined only as 'a group of related steps forming one logical milestone', owned by exactly one deliverable (P0), with example milestones 'data layer, service layer, endpoints'. P0 says a deliverable that needs several milestones gets several phases and a small deliverable may be one phase. There is no maximum number of steps or files per phase, and no instruction to split a phase that grows large.
patterns.name: Size guidance in the plan prompt

snippet.code:
| **Low** | Isolated change in one file, easy revert, no schema or data change, no API-contract change. | 3 to 5 steps, minimal risk section. |
| **Medium** | Several files in one area, or a change to an existing contract, or new integration points. | 5 to 15 steps, risk section with mitigations. |
| **High** | Architectural change, schema or data migration, cross-module change, shared-library change, or change to an external integration. | 10 to 30 steps, full risk matrix, rollback strategy. |

patterns.description: Two lists. The first is the paragraph that begins 'Ostra checks these on every Document call and lists each failure in the result. An error blocks the submit call. A warning does not, but fix it:', in Step 7 (`Write the plan with Document`), `prompt.md` lines 477-487. It names these errors: phases numbered 1..N with no gap or repeat (P10); every `depends_on` names an existing phase; no cycle in the phase graph (P8); every phase has at least one step and a test policy rationale (P12); every step id is `{phase}.{n}`; every `binding_rules` entry names a `constraints` row of the same phase and copies its rule word for word (P13); every step has a `verify` command (P5). It names these warnings: a step with no `delivers` (P11), a delivered requirement not quoted in the phase's `requirements`, a phase that depends on a later phase, and a phase whose deliverable is missing from `deliverables`. The list sits between the Step 7 plan field tables and the 'Pass' line. Right after it, the prompt says what code cannot check and stays with the agent: total delivery of the requirement ledger (P11), the test policy verdict (P12), and self-containment. Other Ostra checks are mentioned outside that list: Step 5 P6 says Ostra refuses the plan when a step names a skill not installed in its repo, or when a phase with code steps names no skill in a repo that has skills; the Step 9 intro says the submit call is refused while the plan has an error, while `step_count` differs from the plan's step count, or while `phases` differs from the plan's phases; Step 7 says Ostra refuses a Write, edit, or shell write to any `ostra-plan-*` file; P7/New projects says Ostra accepts a phase in an unknown project only when `new_projects` names it. The second list is Step 8 (`Run the mechanical pre-checks`), lines 495-557: 8A surviving callers, 8B imports against the target classpath, 8C record results in `pre_checks`, 8D save the spec snapshot. Those are checks the agent runs by command, not checks Ostra runs.

patterns.description: `plan` in `check.rs` emits: unique phase ids, P10 ordering error, `depends_on` unknown-phase error, later-phase warning, missing-deliverable warning, cycle error, and `plan_skills` errors for P6/P7. `phase_body` emits: empty test rationale error (P12), no steps error, duplicate step id, step id prefix error, no-`delivers` warning, unquoted requirement warning, P13 binding-rule errors, empty `verify` error (P5). `check_submit` compares `step_count` with the plan's real step count (check.rs line 697). A grep over `crates/` for step-count limits, max steps, or oversized phases finds no check on the number of steps in a phase or the size of a step. The prompt's list and the code are consistent: neither has a size check. The `Issues` struct has `error` and `warn` methods (check.rs lines 48 and 56), so a warning kind exists for a future check.
